key_insight: Hypersonic Couette flow and flat-plate boundary layers share near-wall SFS stress behavior but differ in outer-layer and heat-flux dynamics because of their distinct thermal structures.
engineering_relevance: Hypersonic large-eddy simulation models should account for flow-dependent thermal structure and filter choice when predicting unresolved momentum and heat transport.
method: Compare filtered DNS of strongly cooled-wall hypersonic Couette flow and a flat-plate boundary layer.
Evaluate top-hat and sharp spectral filters.
Decompose SFS stresses and heat fluxes into resolved, residual, and interaction contributions.
evidence_signal: Filtered DNS shows residual terms dominate mean SFS shear stress and heat flux, while interaction terms contribute with opposite signs in the two flows and boundary-layer SFS heat flux changes sign.
watch_item: SFS magnitudes and features depend strongly on filter choice, so conclusions should not be transferred across filtering strategies without verification.
paper_title: Sub-filter-scale stress and heat flux in hypersonic Couette flow and a flat-plate boundary layer
